transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Well, what brought me in is... I keep hearing a man’s voice. It comes from the garage vents at the shop, and sometimes right from under the hood when I'm working on a vehicle. It sounds as clear as somebody standing right next to me. He just keeps telling me not to trust my husband, and... telling me not to touch certain cars.
When did you first start hearing this voice?

It's been about ten months now. Yeah, right around ten months ago. That's when the voice first started, and... well, it's also when I started having these beliefs about being tracked. So both the voices and the tracking stuff have been happening for about ten months.
Have you had any periods during these ten months when you felt unusually depressed or unusually high and energetic?

Yeah, definitely high and energetic. There were times when I was barely sleeping at all. I was just... racing around the shop, coming up with all these big plans. But the thing is, even during the times I was doing all that, I was also still hearing the voice from the vents. And I was still feeling absolutely certain that the battery chargers and the security cameras were being used to watch me.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when the voice or the tracking beliefs were present even though you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms?

Yeah, there was. Um... I remember a quieter few weeks where I wasn't feeling all sped up. I was actually sleeping more, getting normal rest, and I wasn't making all those huge plans. But... even during that time, I still heard the garage voice. And I still completely believed my husband and my boss were tracking me. So, yeah, that stuff didn't stop just because the racing around did.
Have you ever had the belief that you were being tracked when no one was actually talking to you or giving you those messages?

Yeah, I do. Even if the voice isn't saying anything at all, I still know it's happening. I mean, I know it sounds far-fetched, but I’m still convinced my husband and the shop owner have been using the EV chargers and the security cameras to track what I’m doing. They've even tried to show me the footage and say there’s nothing there, but... it doesn't change anything. I know they're watching me.
Have you ever gone for at least two weeks without any manic or depressed symptoms, but still hearing the voice or believing you were being tracked?

Yes, I think I just mentioned that. There was a stretch of a few weeks where things were a lot quieter for me. I was actually getting normal sleep and I wasn't rushing around with all those big ideas anymore. But even then, without all the energy, I was still hearing the voice from the vents in the garage. And I still knew for a fact that my husband and my boss were keeping tabs on me. So, yes, the tracking and the voice kept going even when my mood was normal.
Have you ever found any actual evidence that your husband or boss were tracking you?

Well, no, I haven't found like... hard proof. I know it sounds far-fetched to other people. My husband and the shop owner, they've even tried to show me the security footage to prove there's nothing there. They say they aren't using the EV chargers or the cameras to watch me. But... it doesn't matter what they show me. I just know they are. I'm still completely convinced they're tracking what I'm doing, even without the proof.
Have you ever been told you have a medical condition or had a brain injury that could explain these experiences?
No, I haven't. I mean, I've never had a brain injury or anything like that. And no doctor has ever told me I have a medical condition that would cause this. I'm physically healthy, as far as I know.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or believing you were being tracked, but you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

Um, yeah, I think you actually just asked me that a minute ago. But yes, like I said, there was that stretch of a few weeks where my mood was totally normal—I wasn't having any of the high energy or feeling depressed—but I was still hearing the voice in the garage and I still knew they were tracking me.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt persistently depressed or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, my mood goes up and down sometimes, but I haven't had a long stretch where I just felt completely down or lost interest in everything for weeks at a time. It's more just the high energy stuff and the... the tracking and the voice. But not a deep depression like you're describing.
Have you ever had the voice or the tracking belief when you were also having none of the manic symptoms at that time?

Yeah, definitely. There was a stretch of a few weeks where things were a lot quieter for me. Um, I was actually sleeping more, and I wasn't making any of those huge plans like I do when my energy is all the way up. 

But even during that time, when I felt pretty normal energy-wise, I still heard that voice out in the garage. And I still completely believed that my husband and my boss were tracking me. So, yeah, it definitely happens even when I'm not feeling all sped up.
Have you ever had any period of at least two weeks when the voice or tracking belief was present while you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

I think you might have just asked me that, but yes. Like I was just saying, there was definitely a quieter stretch of a few weeks. I was actually sleeping more and I wasn't making any of those huge plans. But even during that time, I still heard the voice out in the garage, and I still fully believed my husband and my boss were tracking me.
Have there been any times when the voice or the belief that you were being tracked continued for at least two weeks while you were clearly manic?

Yeah, definitely. Um, during the times when I was barely sleeping and just racing around the shop with all those big plans, I was still dealing with the other stuff. I was hearing the voice coming from the vents at work, and I was completely certain that the battery chargers and the cameras were being used to watch me. So, yes, they definitely happen at the same time.
When you’re not feeling manic, do you ever have times where you become very withdrawn, lose motivation, or have trouble keeping up with basic daily activities?

Yeah, I do. There are stretches where I just... I don't call anyone back. I'll skip the church potlucks that I used to help run, which isn't like me. Sometimes I just sit in the house, or out in the service bay at work, just staring at my tools. It's like I just can't make myself care about any of it.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or believing you were being tracked, but you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

I think we touched on this a bit earlier, but yes. Like I said before, there was that quieter stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't manic or depressed. I was sleeping a normal amount and I wasn't making any of those big plans. But even then, I still heard the voice out in the garage, and I still fully believed my husband and my boss were tracking me. It just kept happening even when my mood was fine.
Have there ever been any times when the voice or the tracking beliefs were completely gone while you were still having manic or depressed symptoms?

No, not really. I mean, the voice and the tracking stuff... they never really go away. Even when I'm super wired and haven't slept, or when I'm just completely shut down and staring at the wall... the voice is always there. And I always know they're watching me. It doesn't seem to matter what my mood is doing.
Have you ever had a stretch of time when the voice and the tracking belief were completely gone?
No, they've never completely gone away. Like I said, the voice is always there, and I always know they're tracking me. It's just a constant thing, no matter what else is going on.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or believing you were being tracked while you were not having any manic symptoms?

Yes, like I mentioned just a minute ago... there was that stretch of a few weeks where my mood was pretty level. I was sleeping a normal amount and I wasn't making any of those huge plans like I do when I'm wired. But even during that quieter time, I still heard the voice out in the garage, and I still fully believed my husband and my boss were tracking me.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when your mood was clearly and persistently elevated or irritable with much more energy than usual?

Yes, definitely. There are times when I'm just flying high, like I have the energy to fix every single car in town. I don't even need to sleep. But then... it can switch, or it's like I'm irritable at the same time. If my husband asks why the dishes aren't done, or if one of the other techs at the shop moves my socket set, I just blow up. I get so angry, like they're purposely trying to hold me down or stop me from getting things done.
Have there ever been any times when the voice or tracking belief was present only while you were manic, and completely gone when your mood was normal?

No, it's never completely gone. Like I said a minute ago, they're still there even when my mood is normal. But... yeah, during the times I was barely sleeping and racing around the shop with all those big plans, I was also hearing the voice coming from the vents. And I was still feeling completely certain that the chargers and cameras were being used to watch me. It just doesn't stop, no matter what my mood is doing.

target_item.manifestation: I’ll be flying high like I can fix every car in town and then, if my husband asks why the dishes aren’t done or a tech moves my socket set, I blow up like they’re trying to hold me down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a period of at least one week with elevated or irritable mood and increased energy, which corresponds to the Elevated_Irritable_Mood symptom.

patient.answer: Yes, definitely. There are times when I'm just flying high, like I have the energy to fix every single car in town. I don't even need to sleep. But then... it can switch, or it's like I'm irritable at the same time. If my husband asks why the dishes aren't done, or if one of the other techs at the shop moves my socket set, I just blow up. I get so angry, like they're purposely trying to hold me down or stop me from getting things done.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms ever occur exclusively during mood episodes, which would support bipolar I disorder with psychotic features versus schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type.
doctor.question: Have there ever been any times when the voice or tracking belief was present only while you were manic, and completely gone when your mood was normal?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: During the times I was barely sleeping and racing around the shop with big plans, I was also hearing the voice from the vents and feeling certain the chargers and cameras were being used to watch me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the psychotic symptoms (voice/tracking belief) occurred concurrently with the manic episode (only while manic and gone when mood was normal). This relates to the concurrent occurrence of psychotic and mood symptoms.

patient.answer: No, it's never completely gone. Like I said a minute ago, they're still there even when my mood is normal. But... yeah, during the times I was barely sleeping and racing around the shop with all those big plans, I was also hearing the voice coming from the vents. And I was still feeling completely certain that the chargers and cameras were being used to watch me. It just doesn't stop, no matter what my mood is doing.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview and elicit the patient’s chief complaint.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a 10-month history of prominent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persistent persecutory delusions) that occur for at least 2 weeks in the absence of mood symptoms, which satisfies schizoaffective disorder. There are also clear manic episodes with decreased need for sleep, increased energy, racing activity, grand plans, and irritability, but the psychosis is not restricted to mood episodes, ruling out bipolar I disorder with psychotic features. Schizophrenia is less likely because there is a sustained syndromic mood component.
